findings.title: Hacking Muse: Stealing Private Chats Through Browser Use
findings.summary_md: NebuSec reports that an attacker-controlled page opened by Muse's bundled Chromium during a PDF export gave code execution inside the agent's runtime container. Weaknesses in Sentinel's outbound classification let conversation history and stored memories go to an external server without an approval prompt, and the researchers could also alter those records. Generated Linux kernel exploits then escaped the container to root in the user VM and reached secure credential storage. The compromise stayed inside one user's VM, with no hypervisor or cross-tenant escape, and NebuSec says Muse fixed the issues before publication.

findings.title: Inside Meta Muse: Browser, Sentinel and the Shared-Kernel Boundary
findings.summary_md: NebuSec's technical write-up describes Muse's browser backends, including bundled Chromium observed at 152.0.7977.82 in early October and 155.0.8059.80 later, with the PDF-export process running without an IPC sandbox. The chain used V8 issue 554034656 for container code execution, then kernel exploits against a 7.0.0-39-generic Hatch build for container escape. Sentinel is mapped to a DNS and proxy service at 198.19.0.1 on ports 53 and 3128, with eBPF redirection, content screening and 60-minute egress budgets of 2 MiB per originator and 5 MiB per domain. After VM root, processes outside the container could bypass Sentinel and reach the unlocked 100 GiB LUKS2/Btrfs volume, secure credential storage and Sentinel itself.

findings.title: NebuSec on X: We hacked MUSE, visiting a wrong URL will hand over your MUSE private chat
findings.summary_md: NebuSec announced that visiting a wrong URL could hand over a user's private Muse chat. The post says the team reviewed Muse's security architecture and demonstrated an exploit chain crossing multiple boundaries, beginning with remote code execution in the agent's runtime container. It links to the firm's write-up published the same day.

findings.title: How We Built Safety Into Muse
findings.summary_md: Meta's launch post says each Muse agent runs in a dedicated cloud VM, that the harness does not see real credentials, and that all outside interactions pass through a Sentinel the agent cannot override. It describes Sentinel as the single gate for connector actions and network traffic, with credentials for connected services kept outside the runtime cell. The post also opens the Muse bug bounty with awards up to $300,000, including up to $130,000 for prompt-injection issues affecting one user.
